utterances.text: Yes. And I mentioned the same thing in providing an answer to you less than five minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you recall the evidence of another former JNA general, Milosav Djordjevic, who gave evidence in this case about his meeting with you in Belgrade at the MOD?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do recall that he testified, although I could not recall the event he discussed. I do remember, though, that he mentioned it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could we have P02300, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer, as I did with Mr. Zivanovic, I will harass you asking for tab numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I've got them right in front of me, Your Honour. I just haven't been saying them. This is tab 1548.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If we could go to paragraph 71, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, this is from the 92 ter statement, the admitted evidence of General Djordjevic who here describes an occasion in November 1991 when you, as president of the government of the SAO SBWS, came to Belgrade to meet Minister Simovic. It continues on. Djordjevic met with you instead. He says you were accompanied by Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, and that you were requesting weapons. Do you recall that meeting with General Djordjevic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall that meeting. I am certain, though, that Arkan did not accompany me. He could only have arrived after me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, that's interesting, Mr. Hadzic, because this is not something that you or your counsel raised or challenged with General Djordjevic when he gave his evidence. You do know that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not understand your question. My consultation with counsel was not so detailed as to discuss with him which item needs disputing and which one does not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So are you now disputing this? Are you saying that General Djordjevic made this up?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have no doubt that he had reasons to lie, but I don't think he could have known whether I came alone or whether Arkan arrived after me or did not. I can't say this with certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, isn't it true that you were involved with Arkan in attempting to procure weapons for armed forces in SBWS on your trips to Belgrade during this period?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: In the last answer, the witness said that Djordjevic had no way of knowing whether Arkan arrived with him or after him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In all of this, the only thing that is true is that I was trying to obtain those shells, but it had nothing to do with Arkan.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could we have tab 1556 which is P02333.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And while that's coming up, Mr. Hadzic, I'll ask if you recall the testimony of the journalist, the Dutch journalist, Mr. van Lynden, who told the Chamber about meeting you and Arkan at a patisserie in the middle of the night in Belgrade. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. And that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could we have P1008, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Tab number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let me skip that one for the moment, Mr. President. Is this the time for the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Indeed, it is, Mr. Stringer. Thank you. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The next exhibit is tab 1041, which is a video at P1008.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Are the interpreters ready?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, we are, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's start then.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, we have this. This is in evidence. It's video footage of a press conference given at the Erdut -- what we call the castle which is the building where your government had its offices in the conference room. Does that appear to be the location?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Do Your Honours wish us to read out the transcript? As the console did not operate at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I -- I was -- I was -- I would say I was a little bit confused and I didn't hear any translation, and then I thought it wasn't necessary. Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, probably the translation is not the most important part. But if it would assist, we could run -- it's a short clip. We could run it again, Your Honour, and hear the translation that accompanies it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks. Let's do that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Borders have already been moved, external and internal ones. Both Krajinas spoke out and you know our big national assembly's decision disrupted its legal continuity with the Republic of Croatia. So, the borders are as they are, and I am in favour of not changing them. Leave them as they are."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, what's indicated on this footage is that Mr. Raznjatovic is also present in the conference room during this. Did he frequently or regularly attend press conferences in the castle facility in Erdut?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I recall, it was very seldom.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you recognise the man who was seated next to you in the footage? We could show it again if you'd -- if you'd like. The man who was seated next to you at the table.

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my left, it was Rade Leskovac. I recognised him.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could we now have, please, tab 1133, which is P00250.245.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, you've testified about this incident in your direct examination regarding the events of the 21st of September, 1991, where, again, we find that you and Mr. Raznjatovic are present at the same place at the same time. Here, each of you taking prisoners from the police station in Dalj. Do you recall that incident?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall the events of 21 September.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And I believe your evidence was that you came there on your own and that Mr. Raznjatovic, Arkan, showed up after your arrival. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. He arrived perhaps ten minutes after me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And was this just another coincidence, then, that you both happened to find yourselves there at the Dalj police station at the same time, or was there some reason why both of you were there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with your words when you say "just another coincidence." It indeed was a coincidence. I came for well-known reasons which I have explained here, and I don't know why Arkan came.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You do know what is the fate of the prisoners that he removed from the police station on that day, don't you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned about that later.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Just earlier today, Mr. Hadzic, minutes ago at page 42, I asked you -- or I suggested that Arkan provided security for you on numerous occasions throughout 1991, 1992, and 1993, and you said that's not true. Isn't it true that he provided security for you to get from Erdut to the Velepromet facility in Vukovar on the 20th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true. He did not provide security for my route from Erdut to Vukovar in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did he provide security --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Stringer. Sorry. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: If he could repeat his answer, because I -- I think that is not accurately transcribed or translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, could you please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for what Mr. Prosecutor said, to the effect that Arkan provided security along the route from Erdut to Velepromet to Vukovar is incorrect. I came there without Arkan of my own accord.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could we please have 65 ter 02320, which is tab 830.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, this is from your testimony under oath as a witness in the Dokmanovic case. Starting with transcript page 3099 of Dokmanovic. At the bottom of 3099, we can go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: This is 65 ter 2320. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The last four lines on this page, Mr. Hadzic, you were asked what was your affiliation with Arkan. You said nothing special. And then on the next page of that transcript, Your Honour asked: "Isn't it a fact that he accompanied you from Erdut on that day driving to Velepromet because you expected some difficulties in getting through to Vukovar?" And you said: "We needed that. It's not that we had to penetrate through the area, but we didn't want any incidents to occur in Vukovar because Arkan had sufficient authority in order to prevent this kind of incident." Isn't that really how it was, Mr. Hadzic? Arkan did, in fact, accompany you from Erdut to Velepromet as security on the 20th of November?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct. As for what I said in the -- in my testimony in the Dokmanovic case, I don't glean from it that I was clearly and distinctly asked about it. I thought they were asking about security at Velepromet. And I don't think I said anything that contravenes what I've said today. I think I've already explained that during examination-in-chief. I did make a mistake though. Although I was under oath, I didn't lie; I simply made a mistake, a technical mistake. I didn't think much about those details. And all my life I went to Vukovar via Borovo Naselje. For 33 years that is how I reached Vukovar. In a sort of mechanical way, I said I went via Borovo Naselje without thinking, but then when I thought about it again, when I -- here, I saw that I went via Erdut to Backa Palanka to pick up Stupar and then we went back from Serbia via the border crossing at Sotin. I didn't need Arkan to provide security for me at Velepromet. I had decided to go there in any case. Other government members, especially Dr. Hadzic, were afraid. They said it They said it would be -- it would not be safe to go there without security.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could we have tab 1085, which is 65 ter 4974.04. This is more transcript from Mr. Hadzic's suspect interview. Looking at page 51 of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, here, we see in the suspect interview you were asked by the investigator, Mr. Dzuro: "Did Arkan and his men provide security for you?" You said: "Not specifically -- specifically. But only in regard to those general assessments when I was in the field. Then he asks you specifically: "After the operations in Vukovar were completed and you went to Vukovar for this government meeting, Arkan went there with you as well. In what [sic] capacity was he there? "Yes, well," you say, "then he went as physical security -- for physical protection. Because I had serious threats from Vukovar, from Serbs ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. DZURO SAYS
utterances.text: "So it is just in one case when he actually did your security, or was it more often?" And your answer is: "It wasn't often but there could have been some other cases. I don't know." So, Mr. Hadzic, isn't it true that, in fact, Arkan provided security for you on the 20th of November, as well as on other occasions?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is not connected with what we just discussed, whether he went with me. I said he didn't go with me. In Velepromet, he was providing security to me and the entire government.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Could you please look at the tab number again because you said 1085, and that's obviously not the 65 ter number that's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We will double-check that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can we agree that Arkan was present with you at the Velepromet facility on the 20th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can agree about that. I just want to ask the Court, considering that before the break we mentioned the meeting with the journalist, van Lynden, and I didn't finish my answer that I saw him there but nothing else. I thought we would continue with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Your counsel can bring you back to that on his redirect examination. This is my cross-examination. I'm going to ask you questions. I think you were given a full opportunity to provide an answer before we had the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And unless the Chamber wants more explanation from you on it, I would prefer, Mr. President, just to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So just to sum this up, Mr. Hadzic, when you testified in Dokmanovic about Arkan accompanying you, or when you were asked about it in Dokmanovic, about his accompanying you to Velepromet, the transcript here is -- is -- doesn't, in your view, reflect what actually occurred. You made a mistake?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time the question was not as precise as the way you put it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, let's go back to it. It seems rather precise to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: This is 65 ter 02320 which is tab 830, page 3100 of the Dokmanovic transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And just for completeness, let's go to the previous page, the bottom. Page 3099. This was your cross-examination, Mr. Hadzic. You were asked: "What was you're affiliation with Arkan?" And you said: "Nothing special. It was said of him he was brave. I don't know anything else." And then the next question, which is on the next page, I'd suggest, Mr. Hadzic, is quite precise. "Now isn't it a fact that he had accompanied you from Erdut on that day, driving to Velepromet, because you expected some difficulties in getting through to Vukovar." And your answer is: "We needed that." And you go on to explain. The fact is that's the truth, isn't it, Mr. Hadzic? Arkan accompanied you from Erdut down to Velepromet, stayed with you at Velepromet, and then, in addition, he attended the meeting that occurred at Velepromet on that day, the 20th. Isn't that all how it really turned out, how it happened?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that this question was already answered. This particular part of transcript was confronted and shown to the witness and he give answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, I think that given the attempt or the -- the response to his -- the comment to his Dokmanovic testimony justifies further examination of this topic and comparing it to his evidence in this trial, which is also under oath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, also for the record, tab 1085 is it. However, the -- the exhibit number is 4974.04.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stringer. It's okay now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could we please have P1971, which is tab 996. Actually, apologies. Before we move on to that, more from Dokmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: In this case, Mr. Hadzic, and I think you've just reaffirmed it a few moments ago, you testified that your counsel asked how did you reach Vukovar on the 20th of November? And you said that you travelled to Vukovar via Backa Palanka and Ilok and perhaps Sid and then in through Sotin. That's at transcript 9754. Is that your evidence now?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct too.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Because in your Dokmanovic testimony - this again is 65 ter 02320, tab 830 - at page 3094, you said something different. The bottom of 3094, this is the beginning of your cross-examination. You're asked about your arrival at Velepromet on the 20th. And at the bottom you were asked: "Where were you before that time on the 20th of November?" This is now on the next page. You said you were in Erdut. You were specifically asked: "What route did you take?" You said: "I didn't really think about it, but I think I came via Borovo Naselje to Vukovar. "Q. Did you go through Dalj and Borovo Selo?" And as you said: "It's only logical, Erdut, Dalj, Borovo Selo, Borovo Naselje, Vukovar." So, according to your testimony in Dokmanovic, which is actually quite a bit closer in time to the events of 20th November, 1991, you remembered it differently. Why have you changed your evidence?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Dokmanovic case I also said I thought I had gone that way. But I later remembered because I was entering from the direction of Sotin. And the first three houses that were razed to the ground that I saw, among them was the house of a friend of mine, and I was shocked and that's how I remembered I came from the direction of Sotin.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You failed to remember that back when you testified in the Dokmanovic case, however, back in 1998; correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked me that already.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You remember it better today than you did back then?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Today I remember it precisely. Back then, I also said I couldn't remember well. If you can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could we now have P1971, tab 996. We don't need transcript for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You can stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, can we agree that that's you and Arkan at the Velepromet facility on the 20th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And he was there providing your security?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not me especially. He was providing security to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could you tell the Chamber, please, the -- about the pins that both of you are wearing on your berets there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like most residents of the Serbian district at the time, we are wearing this flag, red, white, and blue, without any idealogical insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you and Arkan frequently wear what appears to be the same uniform?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure it's the same uniform, but it's similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you frequently wear similar uniforms?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was wearing what I had: The one I have here in this picture and another camouflage uniform. I don't know what Arkan wore all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could we please have P00131, tab 1020.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could we start again, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Can we start again.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] The economy of Belgrade and Serbia is prepared to fully support the Serbs in Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, the mayor of Belgrade, Milorad Unkovic, stated today in Erdut. While talking to the representatives of the regime's government, Unkovic said, among other things, that it was Belgrade's intention to aid reconstruction of destroyed villages and cities in the Serbian region especially Vukovar in the shortest possible time. On the occasion of the Belgrade's delegation visit, president of the Serbian region's government, Goran Hadzic, has assessed that this was one of the signs that people had not been left to themselves, to their own devices."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, we have this as a meeting that occurred in Erdut with the mayor of Belgrade at the time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct. We saw that we was -- he was at that cabinet session, but I didn't see myself there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, here in this footage that we're seeing, you're speaking to the press. Can you tell us who's standing to your right, our left as we look at it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Arkan.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And in what capacity, then, is he standing next to you? What's the reason why he's there with you at this press conference in Erdut?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult for me to answer now, considering that Arkan is dead, and I don't know. I'm not sure whether he was standing there already when I started giving the interview or he came later and stopped there in order to be in the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So could this be one of those occasions you've described where he was just trying to get close to you or was -- tended to follow you around to get close to you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the way it always happened. This is just one more such situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you recognise where you're standing when you're giving this interview?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recognise it. I'm not sure it was even in Erdut or that it is related to that event with the mayor of Belgrade, or perhaps it was just reporter's comment with my picture inserted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could we replay that and get the translation again or the interpretation of the text? It might help us refresh the witness's memory.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] The economy of Belgrade and Serbia are ready to provide full support for Serbs in Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem said Milorad Unkovic in Erdut today. While talking to representatives of this region's government, Unkovic, said, among other things, that it was Belgrade's intention to aid the reconstruction of destroyed villages and cities in the Serbian region, especially Vukovar. In the shortest possible time. On the occasion of the Belgrade's delegation visit, the president of the Serbian region's government, Goran Hadzic, has assessed that this was one of the signs these people have not been left to their own devices. Hadzic said he believed that all Serb lands including Vukovar would shortly be rebuilt and all conditions for normal functioning of important living points all over Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem would be provided in the shortest possible time. With regard to the most recent 14th cease-fire, Hadzic underlined that the Territorial Defence of the Serbian region would respect it but that he doubted the goodwill and intentions of Ustashas, as he called them, who proved that they had had intentions by attacking the liberated Serbian village of Vera and Bobeta."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Having looked at the video now, Mr. Hadzic, can you tell us where this meeting with the mayor of Belgrade occurred?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand you. It's not in dispute that it took place on the premises of the government in Erdut, the room where we held press conferences. And we could see that Dr. Mladen Hadzic, who was vice prime minister, led that cabinet meeting and on his left was Dr. Caslav Ocic and on his right was Mr. Unkovic. What I said was I didn't know where this interview was given. I just don't recognise that building in the background. I don't recognise it from the outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, in the interview, you state -- you underline that the Territorial Defence of the Serbian region would respect the cease-fire agreement. What involvement and knowledge did you have in this 14th cease-fire agreement that enabled you to inform and make a public statement about it being respected by the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard from media reports and the journalists knew about that peace agreement, but I'm not sure I even said that. The journalist added that comment and used the term ‘Territorial Defence.’ I might have said perhaps that the Serbian side had never made any provocations and would not make any provocations. I could not speak on behalf of the Serbian units because I didn't command them. But at that time an incident took place where some of my friends lost their lives in villages Vera and Bobota.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In autumn 1991. It might have been during the winter already.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did Arkan frequently have access to the government press conference room there in Erdut? We've seen him there now twice. Could he just come and go as he pleased?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our press conferences were public and completely open. And if I remember well, there was no particular procedure one had to undergo in order to come in or come out. We didn't even check the accreditations of journalists. And you've asked me before, and I said I don't remember Arkan was there often. In the footage we saw before, we could see him come in and take a chair next to the door. He came in after the beginning of the press conference.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And based on what we've been looking at, Mr. Hadzic, it appears that your own security people whom you've named were no impediments to Arkan actually getting physically close to you, next to you. So they accepted him as someone who could accompany you or at least get close to you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I occupied a political post in 1991, 1992, 1993, and later 1996 and 1997. My security detail never stopped anyone from approaching me, including Arkan. They didn't make any problems. They never stopped anyone from approaching me in Erdut, in Belgrade, or anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could we have tab 1675, please, which is 65 ter 04835.01. This is a video.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could we have a moment? They are not in order.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: While that's being located --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: -- Mr. Hadzic, let me first ask: Do you recall you and Arkan receiving a member of the Australian parliament at the training centre or at the government facilitates in Erdut after the fall of Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember that. It's possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: One moment, please, before you start the video. I wanted to say something about videos and the trouble interpreters might have. In the -- in this trial, the existing system requires that parties, A, provide a transcription of videos, and similar long texts that are prepared in advance; and, B, identify correctly the portions being shown in court. I wonder whether it would be a good idea to add to this general rule that before we start playing videos that need interpretation, we wait for the booth to indicate that they are ready. Okay? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I believe the booth has indicated they are ready now for this next one.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Member of Parliament of New South Wales in the federal state of Australia, Mr. John Newman, visited East Slavonia and Western Srem today. As the head of the delegation of the Serbian National Association's Co-ordination Committee for Liaison with the Australian Parliament and ethnic community at the Labor Party's Main Board, he met with Major-General Andrija Biorcevic in Dalj. This Australian MP, accompanied by the bishop of Slavonia and Baranja, Bishop Lukijan, visited ruined Serbian churches in Vukovar. In Erdut, the guests were welcomed by the line of honour of the Serbian Volunteer Guard and its commander, Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan. At the end of the visit, the Australian deputy talked with Goran Hadzic, president of the government of the Serbian District of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. Mr. Newman stressed he had come to Serbia to get personally acquainted with the political and war events in Croatia where Serbs formed the majority of the population because, as he said, Serbia had a very bad reputation abroad due to the inept propaganda effort which was to be blamed on some political leaders as well. He named Vuk Draskovic and said it would be better for him if he would write books rather than deal in politics."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Having seen the video now, Mr. Hadzic, do you recall this visit?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And based upon the visit to Vukovar and the destroyed churches, it would appear to be sometime after the fall of Vukovar. Do you recall approximately when?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by what I can see, where I received him, and so on, I think it was at the time when I was already the president of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, that is to say, after February 1992. But I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: In what capacity was Arkan then accompanying you as the president of the RSK in this meeting with this Australian member of parliament?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a conflation of arguments. Arkan came with a guest and I understood Arkan as his host. They were at Arkan's place first and then they came to Erdut to the apartment. He came as a member of the ambassador's delegation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Right. My question was about Zeljko Raznjatovic. In what capacity was he acting in connection with this visit?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I have answered, but let me repeat. He came together with the ambassador, the Australian ambassador. Before that, Arkan received him at his centre and then they came to the government building together.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, we tender that exhibit, 4835.01.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3207.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3207. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could we please have tab 440, which is P1836.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: While it's coming up, Mr. Hadzic, this is an exhibit that you talked about during your direct examination. This concerns an incident that occurred at the Vukovar Hospital in the middle of March 1992. Do you recall your evidence about this?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I mostly remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And you gave a detailed account of what occurred. My question simply here is: Whether this is yet another -- well, I'll put it to you. In fact, the role that Arkan played here, on that day, was to provide security for you as the president of the RSK. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So then this is another incident when he just showed up without your invitation and again just trying to get close to you, following you around. Is that how we're to understand it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it only confirms my assertion. And that's the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were you present in Bijeljina in Bosnia-Herzegovina in April of 1992, a couple of weeks after this Vukovar incident, with Arkan, Ms. Plavsic, and other members of the Bosnian Serb leadership?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I wasn't there with Arkan but with Biljana Plavsic and Fikret Abdic. And Arkan was there as a member of Biljana Plavsic's delegation. He had arrived there before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could we please see P00381, tab 1020.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Isn't that the video-clip we just saw, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Forgive me. It is tab 1021.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It's a video-clip, so we'll wait to hear from the interpreters when they are ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We have found it, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Mrs. Plavsic, you are a part of a mixed delegation visiting Bijeljina today to witness the alleged destruction which has been widely reported by the Sarajevo media. What are your first impressions? "I just passed through the town, not just me but my escort as well, and we tried to see whether we would notice any broken windows or shut windows."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, I'm not so interested in the text of what Ms. Plavsic is saying in this video. Can you see on the screen yourself and Mr. Raznjatovic, Arkan, also in the frame with Ms. Plavsic here?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As everyone can see it; I see it too.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And you said just a moment ago that he was there, Arkan was there as a member of her delegation. Could you tell the Chamber, please, in what capacity was he a member of "her delegation," if you know?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry. May I see the reference where the Arkan was named as a member of delegation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm just looking at Mr. Hadzic's answer at page 69, lines 7 and 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is not stated that he was member of delegation, that Arkan was a member of any delegation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Line 7, Mr. Stringer -- sorry, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'm looking at ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, line 7: "And Arkan was there as a member of Biljana Plavsic's delegation ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry. Biljana Plavsic's delegation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But not as the member of delegation who visited Ms. -- Mrs. Plavsic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can try to clarify with Mr. Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And the question -- well, in what capacity was Zeljko Raznjatovic then present at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know in what capacity he was present, but he was there together with Biljana Plavsic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: He was there because he was a key figure in the work being done by yourself in Croatia and the other Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina on establishing and holding the Serb Autonomous Regions. Isn't that why he's there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have said that I don't know why he was there. I know why I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And you were there in order to discuss with your Bosnian Serb counterparts how to go about linking up the autonomous regions in Croatia with the Republika Srpska area taken by Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's not correct. And it's a very improper conclusion. I would understand if you had made such a conclusion had Mr. Fikret Abdic not also been present there, because he was a member of the Bosnian Presidency and a representative of the Muslim people, and I never attended any meeting that was not also attended by Mr. Fikret Abdic, a kind of Serbian meeting. I had come there in order to meet with Fikret Abdic and Biljana Plavsic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: But it was one of your objectives and one of the objectives of those in the leadership of the Bosnian Serbs to actually unify the Serb-held territories in both countries, Bosnia and Croatia; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in your conclusion, you have gone very far right now. My goal was to protect the people, to prevent any deaths, and to remain in Yugoslavia. And what were other goals of other people, this I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So if that was a goal of other people, it's not one that you shared?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure what your question is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If others had as a goal the unification of all the Serb-held territories both in Bosnia and Croatia, is that a goal that you yourself did not share?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have said, first of all, what my goal was. It was that I and everyone else who so wished would remain in Yugoslavia. I think that at the time that was also Mr. Fikret Abdic's goal.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether you supported the idea of unifying Serb-held territories in Croatia and Bosnia. Did you support that or not?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at the time when this event took place, I had no information about this, nor did I talk about it at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could we now have tab 1681, which is 65 ter 4843.1. I believe, actually, it's 1671, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We have it, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Now is not the time for quarrels and divisions but instead for unity, harmony, and for the Serb people living together in one state. That was just one of a series of similar messages from today's gathering at the 17th of August training centre of the Krajina MUP in Golubic near Knin held on the occasion of the start of training of the first class of policemen of the Krajina MUP. Along with a great number of citizens, this activity also attended by members of the Yugoslav Presidency, Sejdo Bajramovic and Jugoslav Kostic, then by Goran Hadzic, Mile Paspalj and Zdravko Zecevic with members of the Krajina government, and by other dignitaries among whom were also representatives of the Yugoslav People's Army."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, do you recall what this event is that we're seeing in the video?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was said it was in a village next to Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Isn't this an event taking place at the Golubic training centre in Knin?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, Golubic near Knin. I said a village. Yes, its name is Golubic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you recall this event? There is quite a number of interesting people there.

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember it. I have seen this video among the Prosecution evidence which you presented with your witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: That's correct. There's a slightly different version that's already in evidence. The reason why we -- we've pulled this one, Mr. Hadzic, is to ask you about, if you can tell us who is seated behind you here in this image.

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recognise anyone behind me except for the person standing behind me, and that was my escort, Ljubomir Mudrinic. And I don't recognise anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, seated to his right, isn't that Arkan?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not certain that that's Arkan. But I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You don't disagree that Arkan was present at this event, do you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't especially notice him, but I don't exclude the possibility. He may or may not have been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, we tender this 4843.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Which is tab 1681, not 16 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: No, 1681; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3208, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could we have tab 922, please, which is P3115.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, you testified --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you're getting scared to give tab numbers, but I'm still asking for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] 922.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, you testified about this document on your direct examination. This is one of the UNPROFOR documents, and it reports the incident that occurred on the Batina bridge in October of 1993. You gave a full account of your recollection of this event. I just wanted to confirm, then, that this is another coincidence when -- or another situation in which Arkan was following you, or trying to be with you, on this occasion as you travelled to Beli Manastir for the RSK Assembly. Is that -- is that how we are to understand what happened here?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what happened here in this context and in connection with me. It has nothing to do with me. It can be interpreted as anyone wants. But I don't see myself there. It happened after my passage, at least 10 or 11 minutes as is written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I guess my point is this is like the incident in Dalj at the police station, and like the incident at the Vukovar in the hospital, where, just by happenstance, or for reasons that you can't explain, you and Arkan are in the same place or passing through the place, the same place, at the same time, or in very close proximity to one another. Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already explained it. He tried to follow me all the time. I'm not sure whether he was following me to Baranja or whether he was going on his business of some sort. He was trying always to follow me so that whenever I was somewhere he could say, Oh you were here or there. It is dangerous. The Croats would kidnap you, kill you, and that sort of intimidation. But anyone can draw any conclusions he or she likes. I have told you what sort of conclusion I'm drawing from this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, in fact, Mr. Hadzic, one could easily draw the conclusion that you and Arkan were very frequently together and that you had a close association based upon the numbers of times now we've already gone through in which the two of you are together at the same place, whether it's in Belgrade, whether it's in Dalj, whether it's in Erdut, whether it's at the hospital in Vukovar, Velepromet. The conclusion one could draw is that the reason for that is because of your close association with him. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. It's a completely wrong conclusion. Because Slavonia and Baranja is a small area. I wasn't there frequently, not every day, and you take out these five or six evens out of the context.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did Arkan follow you into the RSK Assembly meeting on that day, the 9th of October, 1993?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't enter after me. He could enter freely of his own free will. Why would he follow me? There were 200 deputies there. Maybe he followed someone else. I mean, he probably entered, but why would he enter after me?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could we please have tab 714, which is P999.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, these are the -- this is the tape-recording of what's called the first sitting of the second regular session of the RSK Assembly on the 9th of October, 1993, in Beli Manastir. Directing your attention to the bottom of page 2 of the English, which is at the very beginning of the B/C/S as well, the first page. In the beginning, Mr. Paspalj who is presiding opens the session and extends a special greeting to a deputy of the Republic of Serbia, Mr. Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan. Do you recall in what capacity Arkan was attending this RSK Assembly meeting?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot understand that anyone may think that I should have interviewed everyone present and asked them why they came. But you have the best answer here. You have provided it yourself. He was a deputy in the Republic of Serbia and he was probably a guest, I suppose. I know just as much as you do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could we go to page 7 of the English, please. In the B/C/S version, it's the ERN page ending with 9739.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Here, Mr. Hadzic, and we can back up a couple of pages, if you'd like, I'm going to suggest to you that what we're seeing on this page, page 7, is your speech given that day as president of the RSK. And the beginning of the second paragraph, page 7 of the English you say: "Because of the personal conflict between Minister Martic and Commander of the Serbian Volunteer's Guard, Tigers, retreated from Mali Alan and Ustashas took over that very important hill." Now you mentioned this in your direct testimony. And just one brief question, because I know Your Honours are watching the clock, this is the -- a reference to what you testified about on direct when -- because based on something Mr. Martic did Arkan withdrew and there was consequences that followed?

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that it was that something that Martic did on his own in connection with de-mining and withdrawal of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'm not going to ask you about the personal conflict that you refer to between him and Arkan, but I do wish to direct you to the bottom of that same page of the English and this will be my last question, Mr. President. You say: "Pursuant to my constitutional authority and aware of the responsibility before the Serbian people we all share, I make the decision to replace the minister of the interior, Milan Martic, and the chief of the Main Staff." So what's happened here in this assembly session, Mr. Hadzic, it appears that you have now fired your interior minister, Martic, because of this incident or this event that's referred to above in which Arkan and his people withdrew. Is that what happened?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, may the witness see the B/C/S page of this particular document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Could we provide him with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I believe it's on the same page. It was my belief it was on the same page, Mr. President, but if it's not, it's only --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It seems to be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: -- three paragraphs below from what we were just reading before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Do we have to go over the page in B/C/S, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't believe so. For example, I see the word "thank you" at the bottom of the document, and I cannot see it in B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. So let's turn over to the next page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It should be right above where Mr. Paspalj starts speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We are on the correct page now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The question here, Mr. Hadzic, is -- you appear to be firing or replacing your minister of the interior, Martic, as well as the chief of the Main Staff. The question is whether that is linked to or results from the incidents at Mali Alan in which Arkan withdrew.

utterances.speaker: GORAN HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was connected with the incident at Mali Alan when the Croats in the undefended area entered this territory and killed the Serbs. And Martic de-mined the territory at his own initiative and he planned some sort of offensive, but without the knowledge of the Main Staff Commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, that's a good point for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stringer. We'll adjourn for the day. Mr. Hadzic, you stay witness, as you probably know, and still under oath. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 21st day of July, 2014, at 9.00 a.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.04 p.m.,
